evidence: Console.set_window_title writes the OSC 0 title sequence '\x1b]0;{title}\x07' when is_terminal is True and returns True. It returns False for non-terminals (rich/console.py:1154 region; rich/control.py:33). This matches the reference behavior.
On legacy Windows, the title is set via LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title through the renderer (rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56), matching the reference.
Control.title(title) yields a control segment (text '\x1b]0;hello\x07', control [(SET_WINDOW_TITLE, 'hello')]), matching the expectation in the candidate test and the reference test.
The docstring documents the return-value meaning and that Rich cannot restore the title. The reference's docstring is more detailed, but this is not a behavioral requirement.
Shared with the reference, not a candidate-specific gap: the title is not sanitized for BEL or ESC characters, which would terminate the OSC early.
